title: Recipe catalog
description: Every one of the 171 ready-made Soup CLI recipes at v0.77.0 (qwen3.5-4b-dpo and qwen3.5-2b-dpo added, pixtral-dpo retired), grouped by training task: recipe name, base model, size, quantization and what it is, plus how to list, search, show and use them. 169 load through the config schema; the two resident Kimi K2 recipes are marked unavailable and soup recipes use refuses them with exit 3. Notes which recipes stop before training or carry keys the trainer ignores.

headings.title: What a recipe is, and is not
GRPO: reinforcement learning with a verifier

blocks.html:
Recipe catalog

Soup ships 171 ready-made configs at v0.77.0, and this page lists every one of them. The Recipes page explains how to use them; this one is the catalog, grouped by training task. v0.77.0 added two recipes, removed one and marked two unavailable, see What changed in v0.77.0; v0.76.0 added nine, removed six and changed 38 more, see What changed in v0.76.0.

blocks.code:
soup recipes list                      # all of them
soup recipes search qwen --task grpo   # keyword, --task and --size filters
soup recipes show llama3.1-8b-sft      # print the YAML
soup recipes use llama3.1-8b-sft -o soup.yaml   # write it, then: soup train --config soup.yaml

blocks.html:
What a recipe is, and is not

A recipe is a complete soup.yaml for one base model and one task. At v0.77.0, 169 of the 171 load through the config schema with no unknown keys and no refusal, and the other two, kimi-k2-sft and kimi-k2-thinking-grpo, are refused at load because a resident Kimi K2 load is unsupported (see What changed in v0.77.0): that was checked by loading every one. That says the file is valid. It does not say the run works end to end, and it does not say it was trained to a quality target: the data paths are placeholders you replace, a few recipes stop at trainer setup or carry a key the trainer ignores at v0.77.0 (the list below names them), and this page loaded every recipe through the schema without training any of them. Treat every hyperparameter as a starting point, and read the base model's license before you train on it.

The Size column is the base model's total parameter count as the catalog states it (for a mixture-of-experts model, all resident parameters, not the active ones), not a memory figure. Since v0.76.0 a test compares the label of every recipe whose base has a recorded parameter count (all but four bases the Hub has no count for) with that count and allows 0.70x to 1.15x (#1161), so the labels are approximate rather than exact. Nothing checked them before that: through v0.75.2 deepseek-v3-7b-sft listed 7B for DeepSeek-V3-0324 (it now lists 685B, and the 7b in its name still does not describe the size), and glm-4.6-sft, glm-5-sft and minimax-m2-sft listed 9B. N/A means the catalog gives no size; the test pins those 13 recipes by name. Check the model card before you size a GPU. Quantization is the training.quantization the recipe sets (4bit is 4-bit NF4 loading, the QLoRA setup; none means no quantization; 8bit is 8-bit bitsandbytes loading; not set leaves the schema default, which is 4bit). bitnet_1.58 no longer appears: it is refused at config load and its only recipe was removed. Recipes that run on Apple Silicon say mlx in the notes.

What changed in v0.77.0

  • Two recipes added. qwen3.5-4b-dpo and qwen3.5-2b-dpo are text DPO recipes for Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B (modality: text, so the language decoder only). Upstream says their settings are inherited from the existing Qwen 3.5 DPO recipes, and it claims no training or performance result for either (#2129, #2160). None was trained for this page.
  • One recipe removed. pixtral-dpo: its llava rows had no chosen / rejected columns, and v0.77.0 refuses llava and sharegpt4v rows on preference tasks at config load (#1867, #2064). soup recipes show pixtral-dpo and soup recipes use pixtral-dpo now exit 1 with Recipe not found.
  • Two recipes marked unavailable. kimi-k2-sft and kimi-k2-thinking-grpo stay in the catalog, but a resident Kimi K2 load is refused at config load on Transformers 5.x (#2104, #2130). soup recipes show still prints their YAML; soup recipes use prints the reason, writes nothing and exits 3. Kimi-K2-Base and -Instruct are admitted only under training.stream_layers: true, which upstream verified on CPU with a tiny K2-shaped checkpoint only (nothing has been trained on K2); Kimi-K2-Thinking has no supported route. See Recipes.
  • 22 recipes gained training.gradient_checkpointing: true. Since v0.77.0 the key reaches the TRL trainers, and with its default false the grpo, ipo, bco, reward_model and online_dpo tasks train with checkpointing off, where TRL's own default (on) used to apply. Every grpo, ipo, reward_model and online_dpo recipe in the catalog now sets it, so they keep the memory they had (#1923).

What changed in v0.76.0

  • Nine recipes added. kimi-k2.5-dpo and kimi-k2.5-grpo, deepseek-v4-pro-dpo and deepseek-v4-pro-grpo, qwen3.5-35b-a3b-grpo, qwen3.6-35b-a3b-dpo and qwen3.6-35b-a3b-grpo, qwen3.6-27b-dpo and qwen3.6-27b-grpo. Upstream's changelog says the Kimi K2.5 pair is not trained and takes its hyperparameters from the K2.6 recipes. None of the nine was trained for this page either.
  • Six recipes removed. soup recipes show and soup recipes use of any of them now exit 1 with Recipe not found. cogito-v2-sft and gemma3-9b-sft: no compatible replacement base exists for their shipped definitions (#1122). mistral-large-3-sft: Mistral-Large-3 is published in Mistral's native params.json layout with no config.json, which AutoConfig cannot read (#1398). falcon-e-bitnet-sft: quantization: bitnet_1.58 is refused at config load because BitNet training is not implemented (#825). sesame-csm-tts and spark-tts: their raw-audio configs are refused at config load (#265; since v0.77.0 Sesame CSM trains natively, #1769, and the recipe was not restored). See Removed in v0.76.0.
  • Seven base model IDs fixed. devstral-sft, glm-4.6-sft, granite-4-sft, internvl-3-5-sft, kimi-k2-sft, mistral-medium-3-5-sft and voxtral-sft named invalid Hugging Face IDs; the table below shows the IDs they use now (#1122).
  • Two recipes changed path. minimax-m3-sft and mistral-medium-3-5-sft now set modality: vision, because their bases are vision-language wrappers. oute-tts now reads data.format: chatml (pre-encoded codec tokens) instead of raw audio.
  • 23 existing recipes gained lora.dropout: 0.0 (22 MoE recipes that keep moe_lora, and minimax-m3-sft, which kept the line when it dropped moe_lora). peft refuses dropout on the fused 3-D expert parameters of a Qwen3-MoE under transformers 5.x, so with the schema default of 0.05 the LoRA attach fails (#798). If you turn moe_lora on for a MoE base of your own, set lora.dropout: 0.0 as these recipes do.

Before you run one

Loading as a config and running are different things. These are the recipes where the YAML is valid and the run still stops, needs something you have to supply first, or carries a setting that does not do what its name says. Each was checked against the v0.76.0 source, and the points below that name v0.77.0 were checked again at that tag; none was trained to confirm it.

soup recipes verify is new in v0.76.0 and checks one narrower thing for every recipe at once: whether the LoRA adapter the recipe asks for attaches to its base model. It builds the base's architecture on the meta device from its config.json, so no weights are downloaded, but it fetches each config.json from the Hub and needs the training stack installed. It does not look at your data, your memory or whether training converges, and its exit 0 can mean every config was unverified, so read the summary line. Details are on Recipes; soup recipes verify --config soup.yaml checks a config of your own before a long download.

  • Sharding is a launch flag, not a recipe key. Where a description names DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 or ZeRO-3 or FSDP2 (for example llama3.1-70b-sft, qwen2.5-72b-sft, gemma3-27b-sft, qwen3-32b-sft, qwen3.6-27b-dpo, qwen3.6-27b-grpo, deepseek-r1-32b-grpo and llama3-70b-fsdp2) or says multi-node (the DeepSeek V4 Pro, Kimi K2.5 and Kimi K2.6 recipes, among others), the YAML does not select it. Pass --deepspeed zero2, --deepspeed zero3 or --fsdp full_shard, plus --gpus N, to soup train, as the multi-GPU page shows; for more than one machine v0.76.0 adds --nodes, --node-rank, --master-addr and --master-port, see Multi-node launch. llama3-70b-fsdp2 sets use_fsdp2_compile: true, and soup train --config soup.yaml without --fsdp exits 1.
  • Some recipes need something first. llama3.1-8b-ppo loads training.reward_model: ./output_rm, a reward model you train beforehand. llama3.1-8b-longctx sets use_flash_attn: true, which exits 1 without CUDA and the flash-attn package. baichuan-sft sets training.hub: modelscope, so the base model is fetched through ModelScope into ./.soup_hub_cache. minimax-m3-sft loads a processor that is custom code, so it needs soup train --trust-remote-code.
  • MoE recipes and moe_lora. Through v0.75.2 only the SFT and pretrain trainers and the layer-streaming setup read moe_lora. The eight DPO and GRPO MoE recipes in the v0.75.2 catalog (qwen3.5-35b-a3b-dpo, deepseek-v4-flash-dpo, glm-5.1-dpo, kimi-k2.6-dpo, qwen3-30b-a3b-reasoning-grpo, deepseek-v4-flash-grpo, glm-5.1-grpo and kimi-k2.6-grpo) set it anyway. Upstream says they got attention-only LoRA, not what their YAML said, and that on transformers 5.x (which v0.75.2 requires) peft refused the LoRA attach outright for qwen3_moe, so those runs stopped there (#798, #1074). If you ran one of them, re-run. Since v0.76.0 the DPO, GRPO and the other preference and RL trainers read it, so the 15 DPO and GRPO recipes that set it now pass it on, with limits upstream states: since #1421 expert adapters attach through peft's fused-parameter path (target_parameters) on the qwen3_moe, deepseek_v3, glm4_moe, olmoe, qwen2_moe, qwen3_5_moe_text, minimax and mixtral model types, minimax-m3-sft is attention-only LoRA for a different reason (it no longer sets moe_lora, and its YAML comment says it now targets no experts), the Kimi K2.x recipes are untested rather than known-good because no tiny stand-in for that configuration builds in the installed transformers, and upstream's checks ran on tiny random stand-ins on CPU, never on a real 30B-plus checkpoint. moe_aux_loss_coeff: 0.01 in the DPO and GRPO recipes is the default value and at v0.77.0 is still read only by SFT, pretrain and tts: on a DPO or GRPO recipe it does nothing. (Since v0.77.0 a non-default value is refused at load on backend: unsloth and with stream_layers, which apply no MoE auxiliary loss either.)
  • A reward domain that does nothing. deepseek-v3-reasoning, kimi-k2-thinking-grpo and qwq-32b-grpo set verifiable_domain: math beside a reward_fn that is not verifiable, and verifiable_domain is read only by the verifiable reward (still so at v0.77.0), so it does nothing there.
  • Vision-language bases. minimax-m3-sft and mistral-medium-3-5-sft set modality: vision, so SFT loads the vision-language wrapper and LoRA stays on the language tower. The minimax-m3-sft YAML says in a comment that the vision collator supervises every token, prompt included, and that train_on_responses_only is not applied on this path. pixtral-dpo was not usable as shipped through v0.76.1, because its data.format: llava rows carry no prompt, chosen or rejected, which is what DPO reads (#1867). (Since closed in v0.77.0: the recipe was removed and vision row formats are refused on preference tasks at config load, #2064.) The GRPO trainer is still text-only at v0.77.0, so llama3.2-vision-grpo does not use images.
  • Speech and BitNet. Three TTS recipes remain. orpheus-tts-sft and llasa-tts set data.format: audio, the live-codec path (Orpheus needs pip install snac, Llasa the [audio] extra); oute-tts trains on pre-encoded chatml rows, because a raw-audio Oute config is refused at config load (still so at v0.77.0). Sesame CSM trains natively since v0.77.0, but there is no Sesame CSM recipe; see Modality II. There is no BitNet recipe: falcon-e-bitnet-sft was removed, and the export path (soup export --format tq1_0) is the BitNet path that works, see BitNet. whisper-large-v3-ft goes through the generic audio SFT path; for Whisper speech-to-text use whisper-large-v3-asr. deepseek-v3-pipeline validates its pipeline setting and then runs data-parallel.
